text:
jules (PM): Heads-up — need to finalise packaging constraints for Performance Pack launch. Revenue wants clear hard limits + on-demand add-on guardrails. Quick sync?

maya (Revenue): Agree we can't leave burst open-ended. Customers spike unpredictably and we eat cost. Propose: monthly 'burst tokens' + automatic throttling threshold.

patrick (Eng): Real constraint: how do we degrade when burst exhausted? Throttle (queue) or immediate 429? Both have UX tradeoffs.

jules (PM): Proposed structure: Starter / Pro / Performance base tiers. Optional Burst Add-on (N tokens/month @ $/token). Behavior when exhausted: 1) best-effort queue up to 5s, 2) then 429 + billing note. That keeps latencies bounded. Thoughts?

sam (Sales): Sales caution — customers hate hard 429s during demos. Can we offer a 2-week pilot grace window for named enterprise deals?

celine (Legal): Any grace window must have audit logging + explicit contract language that exceptions are temporary and revocable. Also require abuse clause.

patrick (Eng): quick config sketch: 
```json
{
  "tiers": {
    "Starter": {"qps": 2, "tokens": 1000},
    "Pro": {"qps": 20, "tokens": 25000},
    "Performance": {"qps": 200, "tokens": 500000}
  },
  "burst_addon": {"unit": "token", "default_price_usd": "0.0005"}
}
```
This is just illustrative — we need exact numbers after cost model.

maya (Revenue): Nice. Pricing suggestion: price by token + volume discount tiers. Also list a capped monthly spend for Starter customers to avoid runaway billing surprises.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: FYI — canary for billing-metering changes scheduled Thursday 09:00 UTC.

sam (Sales): Another ask from field: on-demand emergency top-ups (one-off purchase via support/portal) — helpful for pilots.

celine (Legal): Top-ups ok if flagged as non-refundable, immediate effect, and recorded on contract addendum. Also ensure they cannot be used to bypass abuse protections.

jules (PM): Launch checklist (minimum):
- API semantics finalized (error codes + headers)
- Billing integration for tokens + refunds behavior
- Contract language for grace windows and top-ups
- Docs + developer examples
- Alerts/monitoring + cost runbooks
- Field pilot with 3 enterprise customers

maya (Revenue): Metrics to track at launch: `cost_per_1M_tokens`, `burst_utilization_%`, `429s_per_day`, `topup_txns_count`. Make dashboard widgets.

patrick (Eng): I'll spec the API responses and the queuing fallback. Expect PR by Wednesday. Will include header `X-Burst-Remaining` and `Retry-After` semantics.

sam (Sales): I'll surface three pilot candidates and collect their minimum acceptable SLA + pilot grace terms. @jules please share one-pager for pilots.

celine (Legal): I'll draft contract snippets for grace windows and top-up terms. Ping if you want redlines for specific customers.

jules (PM): Action items recap: Patrick -> API + headers; Maya -> pricing/volume discounts + capped-starter plan; Sam -> pilot customers; Celine -> contract snippets; Ops -> ensure canary/alerts. Follow-up sync Friday 11:00 PT.

maya (Revenue): +1. Also suggest a small internal experiment: expose a `trial-burst` promo code for new accounts to reduce demo friction instead of blanket grace windows.

patrick (Eng): `trial-burst` seems easier than exceptions. We can add promo code hook to billing + meter. Low dev overhead.

jules (PM): Great — include `trial-burst` in the one-pager. Closing thread — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
